summary: Your own Tailscale control plane: headscale on a VPS behind Caddy, the official Tailscale clients pointed at it, MagicDNS and a deny-by-default ACL, an embedded relay and an exit node, and a restore you performed before switching off the free account.

stack.why: rule zero: do not write a VPN

stack.choice: WireGuard via the official Tailscale clients

stack.why: clients need HTTPS to the control server

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Know that Tailscale is free for six users
prerequisites.why: The honest reason to do this is owning the control plane, not saving money.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. The coordination server needs a public IP.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

prerequisites.name: headscale
prerequisites.get: Download the .deb from github.com/juanfont/headscale/releases and install it on the VPS.

prerequisites.name: The official Tailscale clients on every device
Off-box storage for backups
prerequisites.why: The headscale database is the network's identity.

env.name: BASE_DOMAIN
env.where: MagicDNS base domain; must differ from the server's domain.

phases.title: The server
phases.goal: headscale up behind Caddy with one user.

steps.do: Install headscale, set server_url and the base domain in config.yaml, Caddy in front

check: The health endpoint answers over HTTPS
headscale users list shows your user

phases.title: First two devices
phases.goal: A laptop and a phone reach each other directly.

steps.do: Generate a pre-auth key and register two devices
Ping between them and confirm a direct connection in tailscale status

check: A ping succeeds over the mesh
The connection is direct, not via the VPS

phases.title: DNS and ACLs
phases.goal: Names that resolve and a policy that denies by default.

steps.do: Write an ACL policy denying by default and test a denied port

check: Devices resolve each other by name
An allowed port connects; a denied port is refused

phases.title: Relays and exit node
phases.goal: Hostile NATs still connect; one machine routes traffic.

steps.do: Advertise and approve an exit node

check: A device on a restrictive network still connects
Routing through the exit node changes your public IP

phases.title: Backup and restore drill
phases.goal: The database off the box and a restore that keeps devices connected.

steps.do: Nightly backup of the headscale database and config off the box
Restore into a fresh VPS and confirm existing devices reconnect without re-registering

traps: Until the restore drill is done, keep the free Tailscale account.

phases.title: Operate

steps.do: An update procedure for headscale with a backup first
Uptime on the control server and a reminder for node key expiry

check: An alert fires when headscale stops

product.outcome: A private network whose control plane you own, with a proven restore and a documented upgrade.

operations.backup: Nightly database and config off the box.
operations.incident: If the server is lost without backup, every device must re-register; this is why the drill matters.

notIncluded: SSO with every provider, the admin console, device posture: the seat price, and free for six people anyway.
after: OIDC login via headscale's OIDC support
Subnet routers for a home network
